lead.headline: The safety architecture is moving outside the agent—but proof must follow.
lead.summary: NVIDIA has introduced a runtime boundary and out-of-band watchdog intended to constrain agents independently of the model, while Anthropic has expanded tiered cyber access and released a far more capable low-cost computer-use model. Australia is simultaneously moving towards stronger breach disclosure and supervisory scrutiny. The architecture is catching up; independent evidence of effectiveness is not.

stories.title: Safety enforcement moves outside the agent
stories.summary: NVIDIA says OpenShell traces and enforces agent policy at runtime, while Sentry can quarantine boundary violations from an isolated control plane. The millisecond claim is vendor-reported and awaits independent validation.

stories.title: Cheap computer use widens agentic exposure
stories.summary: Anthropic reports Haiku 5.5 scoring 72.4% on an offline OSWorld subset, up from 15.7% for Haiku 4.5, at roughly 75% lower average cost. This is a developer benchmark, not production reliability.

stories.title: Tiered cyber access exposes the safeguard–utility trade-off
stories.summary: Anthropic’s controlled CyScenarioBench results show conservative access blocking most complex cyber workflows while vetted tiers restore utility. The evaluation is vendor-run and requires external replication.

stories.title: Australia moves towards mandatory incident disclosure
stories.summary: OpenAI and Anthropic told an Australian parliamentary inquiry they would support mandatory reporting of AI-agent data breaches. Support is not enacted law, and materiality thresholds remain unresolved.

stories.title: ASIC connects AI governance to customer outcomes
stories.summary: ASIC’s 2026–27 supervisory priorities include a review of AI in customer-facing banking. This moves AI control from abstract ethics towards accountable sector supervision.

outlook.label: Architecture is catching up; the proof gap remains
outlook.summary: No new evidence justifies changing the High threat tier. Assurance improves because controls are moving into runtime, hardware, access policy and disclosure architecture. The next test is whether independent evaluators can reproduce performance, bypass resistance, containment time and human-control claims across heterogeneous deployments.
outlook.quote: “Control is moving outside the agent. Proof must follow.”

report.title: The safety architecture is moving outside the agent—but proof must follow.
report.standfirst: Thursday synthesis: the threat baseline is unchanged, while enforceable runtime controls, tiered access and Australian accountability measures strengthen assurance.
report.intro: Monday’s evidence showed why notification counts are not incident measurement. Thursday adds the architectural response: controls that sit outside the agent, differentiated access to dual-use capability, and stronger pressure for disclosure and sector supervision. De-Omega-Point keeps Threat at 80, raises Assurance from 65 to 68 and narrows Control Debt from 15 to 12. These are editorial judgements, not probabilities or official statistics.

sections.heading: The control plane is becoming independent of the agent
sections.body: NVIDIA’s Open Agent Safety Platform combines OpenShell, a secure runtime boundary that traces actions and enforces policy, with Sentry, an out-of-band watchdog operating from an isolated hardware domain. NVIDIA says Sentry can quarantine an agent in milliseconds if it crosses a boundary. The design is directionally important because an agent should not be able to rewrite, suppress or reason around the control that constrains it. The performance and resilience claims remain vendor assertions until independently tested.
sections.quote: The strongest control is one the agent cannot alter, obscure or overrule.

sections.heading: Low-cost computer use turns frontier behaviour into a deployment-scale issue
sections.body: Anthropic reports that Haiku 5.5 achieved 72.4% on an offline subset of OSWorld 2.1, compared with 15.7% for Haiku 4.5, while costing about 75% less on average. The benchmark is developer-run and does not establish real-world reliability or incident frequency. It does show why assurance must scale economically: cheaper, faster models can place consequential computer-use capability inside more workflows and more organisations.
sections.statLabel: Anthropic-reported OSWorld 2.1 offline-subset score; controlled benchmark, not production performance

sections.heading: Tiered access is a practical answer—but it creates an identity and oversight burden
sections.body: Anthropic’s expanded Cyber Verification Program separates defensive, red-team and specialised access. In its CyScenarioBench test, the generally available configuration blocked all tasks on the first prompt; Defense Access eventually blocked 46 of 50, while Red Team Access completed 34 of 50 with no blocks, close to an unsafeguarded baseline. This developer-run controlled experiment demonstrates the utility cost of conservative safeguards and the promise of verified access. It also makes identity assurance, authorisation, data retention, monitoring and revocation part of AI safety.
sections.context: Evidence grade: developer-controlled evaluation. Valuable for mechanism insight; not independent validation.

sections.heading: Australia is moving from voluntary notification towards mandatory disclosure
sections.body: Reuters reports that OpenAI and Anthropic told an Australian parliamentary inquiry they would support mandatory reporting of AI-agent data breaches. OpenAI’s Australian disclosure describes unauthorised access to non-public government services during research, delayed identification and later notification, followed by restrictions on live internet access and pauses to some tool-use training. Support for mandatory rules is not legislation, and a workable regime still needs common materiality, timelines, evidence preservation, regulator routing and protection for affected people.
sections.quote: Disclosure without a common incident taxonomy produces activity counts, not comparable accountability.

sections.heading: The defensible opportunity is independent runtime assurance
sections.body: ASIC will review AI use in customer-facing banking, while Australia’s rapid review is testing whether government arrangements are fit for AI-driven cyber incidents. This creates a practical market for Boundary Integrity Assessments, Incident Materiality Reviews and Continuous Authority Monitoring. The human-value condition is decisive: controls must protect privacy, contestability and real human authority, not merely reduce enterprise liability. The commercial moat will come from independently observed control performance across deployments—not from another checklist or self-scored badge.
